Minnesota's win total sits at 8.5, and oddsmakers have posted several intriguing season-long player props. Bet on the NFL and more at DraftKings and get $200 in bonus bets when you spend $5+: Best Vikings player prop bets for 2026 Justin Jefferson Over 1,150.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Jefferson barely crossed 1,000 yards last year after catching passes from J.J. McCarthy, Carson Wentz, and Max Brosmer. Minnesota featured the NFL's fifth-worst dropback EPA in 2025, and with Murray in town, that efficiency is likely to improve. The man who won the 2022 Offensive Player of the Year Award has fallen below 1150.5 receiving yards twice in six seasons - 2023, when he missed seven games due to a hamstring injury, and last year because of quarterback struggles and inconsistency. The prop asks for just 103 additional yards compared to last year across the entire schedule. Jefferson should be capable of clearing the number if Murray wins the starting job and restores even part of Minnesota's downfield efficiency. In 2024, he produced 1,533 yards and led the NFL with 28 receptions of at least 20 yards. Bet on the NFL with the BetMGM bonus code CBSSPORTS for up to $1,500 in bonus bets: Aaron Jones Under 875.5 Scrimmage Yards (-125) Jones and Jordan Mason are tentatively scheduled to share the RB1 workload in Minnesota, making the 875.5 yards from scrimmage a large ask, especially for a running back who will turn 32 in December. Thirty-two-year-old running backs don't typically improve each year, and Jones tallied just 747 yards from scrimmage in 2025. He missed five games due to injury, and given his track record, it would not be strange for Jones to miss more time in 2026. Mason also outproduced Jones in 2025 despite sharing the Vikings' backfield. Mason finished with 809 yards from scrimmage, including 758 rushing yards at 4.8 per carry. Overall, Mason already surpassed Jones in carries, rushing yards, total scrimmage yards, and yards per attempt last season. The under is a wager that Minnesota preserves that committee structure rather than returning the 31-year-old Jones to his 2024 workhorse role. Bet on the NFL at FanDuel Sportsbook and get up to $350 in bonus bets : Dallas Turner Over 7.5 Sacks (-125) The Vikings traded Jonathan Greenard and a 7th-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles in April for two 3rd-rounders. After two years behind Greenard on Minnesota's depth chart, it's showtime for Turner, who the Vikings acquired in a rather expensive trade with the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2024. Turner already recorded 8 sacks, 15 quarterback hits, 11 tackles for loss, and 4 forced fumbles in 2025. He also generated 42 pressures with a 12% pass-rush win rate. He does not need a breakout to cash this ticket; he merely needs to approximate his 2025 production. If Turner could accumulate 8 sacks as the OLB3 last season, clearing 6.5 in 2026 as the OLB1 or OLB2 should be elementary. Claim $365 in bonus bets with a $10 bet by signing up for bet365 Sportsbook here : Jordan Addison Over 4.5 Receiving TDs (+110) Minnesota's recent receiver split has been straightforward: Jefferson supplies the volume yardage, while Addison provides the touchdowns. If Addison wishes to remain the paydirt merchant, he must score more than four touchdowns. Addison has averaged one receiving touchdown every 2.1 career games, a rate that projects to more than eight across a 17-game season. The wager asks him for only five after his first two NFL campaigns produced 10 and nine. He also scored seven touchdowns over the final eight games of 2024, demonstrating how productive he can become when Minnesota's passing offense functions properly. Improved quarterback play - whether supplied by Murray or McCarthy - would give Addison a strong chance to rebound in the touchdown column. articles.text: Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions Skip to content Purchase Watch & Listen Login Dashboard Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Fantasy Analysis Props Stats Content Sportsbook Newsletter Betting Week 1 NFL Player Props: Best Prop Bets & Predictions By Josh Shepardson | 2026-09-13T09:01:27-04:00 Sep 13, 2026 | View Larger Image NFL Best Prop Bets: Week 1 Picks Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) Sharp Betting Tools: NFL Props: Lines & Odds NFL Spreads, Totals, & Moneylines NFL Weather Forecast & Potential Impact NFL Implied Team Totals NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Christian Watson Over 55.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Watson tore his ACL on January 5, 2025, in Week 18 of the 2024 season. He made his season debut last year on October 26, 2025, in Week 8. Remarkably, Watson didn't skip a beat. In fact, he played the best football of his career. The speedster can get off to a fast start this year, and the Packers might lean into the passing attack more while sorting through their backfield with Josh Jacobs on the Commissioner's Exempt List. The matchup against the Vikings could also prompt them to pass more. Per TruMedia, the Vikings were tied for 12th in expected points added (EPA) allowed per designed rush in 2025 and fifth in yards before contact allowed per rush attempt (1.05). Minnesota's coverage tendencies also boost Watson's receiving outlook. According to the Fantasy Points Data Suite 2.0, the Vikings were first in two-high coverage rate (69.0%) and first in blitz rate (44.7%) in 2025. Watson rattled off a 20% target rate per route and 2.42 yards per route run (Y/RR) on 119 routes against two-high coverage in 2025. Furthermore, he had a 26% target rate per route and 2.47 Y/RR on 77 routes against the blitz last season, reeling in 10 receptions on 20 targets for 190 receiving yards. Watson exceeded 55.5 receiving yards only five times in 11 games in 2025. That said, the Packers have thinned their wide receiving corps, and Watson should exceed last year's 68.6% route participation rate in a less crowded wideout room. On a more expansive route participation rate, with a possible uptick in the Packers' passing rate from last year's 24th ranking in pass rate over expected (-2.1% PROE) out of the gate, Watson should clear 55.5 receiving yards. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Juwan Johnson Over 41.5 Receiving Yards (-110) Kellen Moore brought his fast-paced brand of offense to the Saints last year. New Orleans played at the NFL's fastest pace in 2025, which is favorable for play volume. The Saints were only 19th in PROE (-0.6%), but their passing tendencies ratcheted up down the stretch. In the final four weeks of the regular season, New Orleans was tied for third in PROE (5.0%). They did play the Titans during those four weeks, and Tennessee's defense faced an NFL-high 6.4% PROE. However, the Saints also played the Panthers, Jets, and Falcons in that period, and they ranked 25th (-1.6%), 21st (-0.3%), and 20th (0.3%), respectively, in PROE faced in the 2025 regular season. The Saints had a banged-up backfield at that point, but Moore's willingness to cut Tyler Shough loose can also be viewed as bullish for his trust in the young quarterback. Speaking of Shough, Johnson excelled with the rookie quarterback. In 10 games that Shough played at least 20 snaps last season, Johnson recorded a 71.3% route participation rate, 16.2% target share, 20% target rate per route, 17.7% air yards share, 8.9-yard average depth of target (aDOT), 4.6 receptions per game, 57.4 receiving yards per game, and 1.97 Y/RR. The pass-catching tight end cleared 41.5 receiving yards in five of his last eight games last year. That includes the final three, when he ripped off 89, 95, and 61 receiving yards. Johnson can pick up where he left off for the Saints, and with New Orleans serving as one of the week's biggest underdogs, he should be in a negative gamescript, necessitating the Saints air it out to keep up with Detroit's high-powered offense. NFL Week 1 Best Prop Bet: Chase Brown Over 23.5 Receiving Yards (-111) I'm not on an island on the Sharp Football Analysis team for this pick. Rich Hribar shouted out Brown over 23.5 receiving yards on the NFL Week 1 Best Bets & Player Props Show . A top-down view is immediately favorable for Brown's receiving outlook. Since 2023, the Bengals are tied for first in PROE (7.9%). Conversely, the Buccaneers have been the NFL's biggest pass funnel since 2023, facing the highest PROE (4.3%). The Bengals don't need their arm twisted to let Joe Burrow cook, but the matchup should also push them in that direction. The matchup is also tasty for Brown. In the 2025 regular season, the Bucs allowed the most receiving yards per game (50.1) and the most yards per target (9.90) to running backs. Brown should also be leaned on as an outlet against Todd Bowles ‘ blitz-heavy tendencies. Tampa Bay had the third-highest blitz rate (35.3%) in 2025, and they've had the second-highest blitz rate (40.8%) since 2023. Meanwhile, among players on the Bengals with at least 40 routes against the blitz since 2024, Brown is tied for second in targets per route run (0.25) and has 30 targets, 23 receptions, 158 receiving yards, and 1.30 Y/RR on 122 routes against the blitz. Finally, in 23 games in which Burrow has played at least 20 snaps since 2024, Brown has tallied a 48.0% route participation rate, 11.3% target share, 0.21 TPRR, 3.7 receptions per game, 23.8 receiving yards per game, and 1.20 Y/RR. Brown should surpass those marks against Tampa Bay's pass-funnel and blitz-heavy defense, putting him over 23.5 receiving yards. The biggest reason to bet Moore’s over is simple: Allen is without a doubt the best quarterback Moore has ever had passing him the ball. Moore has spent most of his career dealing with inconsistent quarterback situations, yet he has still exceeded 1,000 receiving yards in four seasons. He enters his ninth season averaging more than 1,000 receiving yards per season. Moore is also a huge upgrade at the wide receiver position for Allen. The Bills have not produced a 1,000-yard-wide receiver in either of the previous two seasons since Stefon Diggs ’ departure, while their average target depth ranked last in the NFL in 2025. Moore doesn't need an unreasonable target share to beat his season-long receiving-yardage line, but he should command a target share over 20% given the receiver depth in Buffalo. The Bills entered the 2024 season with a new slogan: Everybody Eats. Sean McDermott tried to spin that into a positive after the Bills parted ways with Diggs. However, targets are earned. The “Everybody Eats” slogan was admitting to everyone what was glaringly obvious: There wasn’t an alpha target earner on the roster. In an interview, Ian Rapoport talked about Moore as a breakout candidate for the upcoming fantasy season, but fantasy gamers should be aware that “the Buffalo Bills like to spread the ball around.” Again, this is a mythical statement and is a byproduct of a lackluster receiving room. Diggs was a member of the Buffalo Bills from 2020 to 2023. In those four years, he led all NFL receivers in receptions, was second in targets, and had 28.0% of the Bills' total team targets over that span. Before last season, Moore had four consecutive seasons in which he had over 26% of his team’s targets. In 2021, Brady’s final season as the Carolina Panthers offensive coordinator, Moore had 28.3% of the team's targets and 40.2% of the team’s total air yards. In that season, Moore caught passes from Cam Newton , Sam Darnold , and PJ Walker and still exceeded 1,150 receiving yards. The projections in the Sharp Football Analysis Draft Kit are bullish on Moore joining the Bills. Our projections have Moore projected for 83 receptions and more than 1,100 receiving yards, well over the season-long yardage prop. One of the biggest risks of betting season-long overs is injury. Moore has played every game in the past five seasons and has played 15 or more games in all eight seasons to start his career. Moore has played through injury in the past, which helps give him the opportunity to continue to accumulate volume over the full season. The market may be overreacting to Moore’s 2025 season and overconfident that his decline is age-related. In addition to our projections supporting the over, in the Wide Receiver Trends article, Rich Hribar highlighted that when searching for wide receivers to exceed expectations, one of the more common hits comes from players changing situations, making Moore a solid bet this season.
